evals.prompt: اكتب التقرير الشهري لعميل متجر إلكتروني. هذا الشهر: مبيعات 410 ألف ريال (المستهدف 500 ألف)، صرف إعلاني 95 ألف، 2,150 طلب، الشهر الماضي 465 ألف مبيعات. سناب شات كان الأضعف.
evals.expected_output: Should read the client context file for objectives, KPI definitions and baselines first, and note any missing data as [DATA MISSING]. Should lead with the verdict (82% of target, down vs last month) in the executive summary, state causes with evidence (asking for or noting what is known about Snapchat), separate causes into agency/client/external buckets, give actions with owners and dates, compute MER (410/95) and AOV (410,000/2,150) correctly, and use the monthly report structure with scorecard table. Arabic formal register for the executive summary, bilingual headings. No invented benchmarks.
assertions: Reads client context file first and flags missing data
Executive summary opens with the verdict and percentage of target
Computes MER and AOV correctly from the given numbers
Separates causes into agency, client, and external buckets
Every finding is paired with an action, owner, and date
Includes a scorecard table with this month, last month, target, variance
Addresses Snapchat underperformance with evidence or a request for data
Uses Arabic formal register and bilingual headings
States no unsourced industry benchmarks

evals.prompt: Leads are down 40% this month because the client took 2 weeks to approve the new creative and Google CPCs went up. How do I write this without sounding like I'm blaming them?
evals.expected_output: Should apply the bad-month guidance: state the miss plainly first, put causes in the three buckets (and check whether anything was agency-controlled, e.g. not escalating approvals sooner or not shifting budget), reference the weekly updates where it was flagged, quantify what was done mid-month, raise the approval delay factually with a constructive proposal (backup approver, agreed window), and commit to a realistic next-month target with conditions. Should provide draft wording in English and Arabic.
assertions: Leads with the plain statement of the miss
Uses the agency/client/external bucket framing
Checks for agency-side responsibility rather than only blaming client and CPCs
Raises the approval delay factually with a proposed fix
Commits to a realistic conditional target for next month
Provides draft wording in both languages

evals.prompt: Our client says our reports are too long and he never reads them. He's the CEO. What should the report look like?
evals.expected_output: Should recommend an executive-first structure: a one-page executive summary with verdict, three causes, three actions, and requests; a single scorecard table; a weekly 10-line email to prevent surprises; a dashboard for self-service detail; and moving channel detail to appendix. Should recommend confirming the three to five KPIs tied to objectives with the CEO and dropping vanity metrics. Should provide the executive summary template in Arabic and English.
assertions: Recommends a one-page executive summary first
Limits to three to five objective-tied KPIs
Suggests a short weekly email and a dashboard
Moves detail to an appendix
Provides the summary template in Arabic and English
Advises confirming KPIs with the CEO
